summary: Princess Juliana International Airport (SXM) is located on the Dutch side of the Caribbean island of Saint Martin/Sint Maarten and is world-famous for its dramatic low-altitude approaches over Maho Beach, where arriving aircraft pass just meters above sunbathers and beachgoers. The airport serves as one of the busiest Caribbean hubs and was heavily damaged by Hurricane Irma in September 2017 before being rebuilt and restored to full operations. Its unique beachside approach has made it one of the most photographed and visited airports in the world.
faqs:
Q: Why is Princess Juliana International Airport so famous?
A: SXM is renowned for its low-approach landings over Maho Beach, where large jets fly just 10-20 meters above the heads of beachgoers, making it a top destination for aviation enthusiasts and plane spotters.

Q: What happened to the airport after Hurricane Irma?
A: Hurricane Irma caused catastrophic damage in September 2017, destroying the terminal and infrastructure. The airport underwent a major reconstruction and reopened with a modernized terminal in late 2017 and 2018.

Q: Which airlines operate from SXM?
A: Major carriers serving the airport include American Airlines, Delta, JetBlue, KLM, Air France, United, Spirit, and Caribbean regional airlines, offering connections to North America, Europe, and other Caribbean islands.

Q: Is the airport safe for such low approaches?
A: Yes, the approaches are carefully calibrated by experienced pilots and air traffic controllers. The beach has designated viewing areas and a famous arrivals board, though standing in the direct path behind the jet blast is extremely dangerous.
transport_tips: Taxis are the primary mode of transport from SXM and are available 24/7 outside the terminal; fares are fixed by zone and can be confirmed at the dispatcher's booth before departure. Rental cars are readily available but driving on the right side of the road with narrow local streets requires caution. Shared shuttle services and minibus options connect the airport to both the Dutch and French sides of the island at lower cost than private taxis.
local_tip: Visit the Sunset Bar & Grill on Maho Beach for the full SXM experience—you can watch arrivals with a cocktail in hand while a live arrivals board shows incoming flight numbers, and on Wednesdays they host a popular Maho Beach party after the last landing.
